standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of presentation along a complete devissage
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label remark-finite-presentation, invoked at proof line 3249
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies that the first module of the devissage is finitely presented over the first algebra, which is what lets the induction be set up on the first step.

standard_prerequisites.name: The finitely presented induction step
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-induction-step-fp, invoked at proof line 3251 and claimed separately as S14-algebra-induction-step-fp
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that after inverting an element outside the given prime the first map of the devissage is universally injective over the base, which is the reduction that makes the induction hypothesis applicable.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of the cokernel of a universally injective map over a domain, and projectivity of the smooth pieces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-ui-flat-domain (proof line 3257); Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian (proof line 3268)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first shows that the cokernel of the first map is flat over the base, so that the tail of the devissage applies to it; the second shows that the smooth algebra appearing in the decomposition is projective over the base, which gives the final projectivity statement.

core_obligations: Reduce to the first step: the assertions concern only the structure of the module over the base, so one may replace the module by the first module of the devissage, regarded as a module over the first algebra; by the finiteness of presentation remark that module is finitely presented (proof lines 3243-3250).

Apply the induction step after localising: by the finitely presented induction step there is an element outside the given prime whose inversion makes the first map of the devissage universally injective over the base (proof lines 3250-3254).

Prepare the induction: since both the source and the target of that map are flat and finitely presented over the relevant rings, the cokernel is flat over the base and finitely presented over the first algebra, and the tail of the devissage is a complete devissage of that cokernel, so the induction hypothesis gives, after a further localisation, a decomposition of the cokernel and its projectivity (proof lines 3254-3264).

Conclude: the first module is the direct sum of the free module and the cokernel, which gives the claimed decomposition; projectivity follows because the first algebra is projective over the base by the non Noetherian projectivity lemma, and the cokernel is projective by the induction hypothesis (proof lines 3265-3269).
proof_roadmap: Replace the module by the first step of the devissage (proof lines 3243-3250).
Localise so that the first map is universally injective and check flatness of its cokernel (proof lines 3250-3258).
Apply the induction hypothesis to the cokernel and assemble the decomposition and projectivity (proof lines 3259-3269).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a finitely presented module flat over the base which admits a complete devissage over a prime becomes, after inverting one element outside that prime, a direct sum of powers of smooth algebras with geometrically irreducible fibres, and is projective over the localised base (statement lines 3228-3241, tag 05IB). The proof is an induction on the length of the devissage: it reduces to the first step, localises so that the first map becomes universally injective, checks that its cokernel is flat and finitely presented so that the induction hypothesis applies to the tail, and then assembles the decomposition and the projectivity from the two pieces. The induction with its two successive localisations is the substance, so the claim is H2.
